title: Linux hacking part 12: LD_PRELOAD function interposition. Simple C examples
content_md: ﷽ Hello, cybersecurity enthusiasts and white hackers! In the previous part , we looked at redirecting a function call through the GOT/PLT. This time, let’s return to LD_PRELOAD and look more closely at function interposition: a shared library can provide a function with the same name as one used by a dynamically linked program. We will build a small directory-listing program and a library that wraps readdir() . The wrapper will log every entry and then return it unchanged. We will compare that log with the program output and with the getdents64 system call shown by strace . The lab demonstrates where an interposed function sits in the call path without changing files or hiding entries. concept The dynamic linker loads shared objects before starting a dynamically linked program. LD_PRELOAD asks it to load a specified shared object before the program’s ordinary dependencies, which lets symbols in that object take part in symbol resolution. LD_PRELOAD is ignored or restricted in secure-execution mode, so the behavior depends on how the program is started. See ld.so(8) . An interposer can call dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "readdir") to find the next definition of readdir() after its own. It can then inspect the result
